specificPurposes.name: english For Development Studies
specificPurposes.targetAudience: Professionals and students in Development Studies who are non-native English speakers.
specificPurposes.description: This course covers a multidisciplinary program that includes anthropology, sociology, world geography, political science, international relations, and gender studies, with a focus on the fundamentals of development.
goals: Increase the learner's range of vocabulary and technical terms in development studies.
Practice and increase comprehension of development texts and international economic and financial terms.
Develop confidence in communicating in a variety of situations with colleagues, business partners, and on political and social platforms both in speaking and writing.
Extend the knowledge of international development systems.
specificPurposes.methodology: A broadly communicative and interactive methodology and a text and task-based approach are used. Reading texts are authentic or semi-authentic and provide context for rural, national, and international development.
specificPurposes.areasCovered: The course covers areas such as the power of language, language skills development, and the use of English for different branches of development studies.
specificPurposes.requiredLevel: Intermediate to upper intermediate level of English as a second language or the equivalent.

specificPurposes.name: legal English
specificPurposes.targetAudience: Lawyers, law students, and professionals who are non-native English speakers with a focus on the fundamentals of international legal English of Anglo-Saxon and Anglo-American jurisdictions in practice.
specificPurposes.description: This course aims to increase the learners' range of legal English vocabulary and comprehension of legal texts in various areas of law with a hands-on approach.
goals: Increase the learners' range of legal English vocabulary.
Practice and increase comprehension of legal texts in various areas of law with a hands-on approach.
Develop confidence in communicating in applied Legal English Language, both in speaking and writing.
Extend the knowledge of international Legal English practice.
specificPurposes.methodology: A broadly communicative and interactive methodology and a text and task-based approach are used. Reading texts are authentic or semi-authentic and provide context for International English Legal vocabulary.
specificPurposes.areasCovered: The course covers areas such as the power of language, the characteristics of legal language, language skills development, and the use of English for different branches of law such as commercial, human rights, family, labor, and international law.
specificPurposes.requiredLevel: Intermediate to upper intermediate level of English as a second language or the equivalent.

specificPurposes.name: english for trade union studies
specificPurposes.targetAudience: Trade unionists and students in trade union and labor studies who are non-native English speakers.
specificPurposes.description:
This course is aimed at trade unionists and students in trade union and labor studies who are non-native English speakers. It covers a multidisciplinary program that includes labor policies, development strategies, labor response to the challenges of globalization, ILO conventions, worker´s and trade union´s rights, social justice, and workers enterprises. 
 The course focuses on the history of the worker´s movement around the world and the use of English as lingua franca in the construction of international worker´s solidarity.
goals: Increase the learner´s range of vocabulary and technical terms in workers struggle history, international labor standards, multinational companies, development policies, and research cooperation on global labor issues.
Practice and increase comprehension of the literature of the worker´s struggle.
Develop confidence in communicating in a variety of situations with colleagues, on political and social platforms both in speaking and writing.
Extend the knowledge of international workers solidarity.
specificPurposes.methodology: A broadly communicative and interactive methodology and a text and task-based approach are used. The reading texts are authentic or semi-authentic and provide context for worker´s emancipation.
specificPurposes.areasCovered:
The course covers areas such as the power of language, language skills development, the use of multilingualism in building workers solidarity.
(A detailed syllabus is available when you join the course.)
specificPurposes.requiredLevel: Intermediate to upper intermediate level of English as a second language or the equivalent.
